q: An order restricting pamphlets is defended as a welfare measure. What is the first question to be asked?
options: Whether the order is traceable to a law capable of imposing a restriction
Whether the welfare objective is one recognised by the Directive Principles
Whether the person affected has exhausted the departmental remedy available
Whether the order has been approved by the district magistrate concerned
expl: A restriction must first be by law; only then does the ground fall for examination.
why: The remaining options are steps that may matter later or not at all, and none is the threshold question.
trapnote: Sequence matters: law first, listed ground second, reasonableness third.

q: A note states that a constitutional amendment is ordinary law and therefore void if it abridges a fundamental right. What kind of error is this?
options: An inversion: amendments were brought within the bar in 1971
An omission: amendments are within the bar only if they damage the basic structure
An anachronism: the bar was abolished altogether by a later amendment
A half-truth: amendments were expressly taken outside the bar in 1971
expl: The 1971 amendment excluded constitutional amendments from the bar.
why: The third option mixes the two doctrines, applying the basic structure test through the wrong provision.
trapnote: Two separate checks exist. The bar was switched off; the basic structure limit was switched on.

q: A press restriction and a welfare-labelled order restricting a meeting are challenged together. Which statement is correct?
options: The press restriction is tested; the welfare order is immune as policy
Both are immune, welfare being fundamental in the governance of the country
Both are tested against the listed grounds, the welfare label adding nothing
The welfare order is tested; the press restriction is immune as free expression
expl: Every restriction faces the same test; labelling does not alter the analysis.
why: The second and fourth options each immunise one limb, which is how selective reasoning is usually tested.
trapnote: The same test applies to every restriction. Labels do not create exemptions.

q: Migrant children are out of school, cannot move freely for want of documents, and are told no remedy exists. Which chain is correct?
options: All three limbs are directives, enforceable only through legislation for the purpose
Schooling is a right, movement is a citizens' freedom, and the writ remedy remains available
Schooling is a directive, movement is a right, and no writ lies for either limb
All three limbs are rights, each enforceable only in the Supreme Court
expl: The limbs fall into different categories and the remedy is not extinguished by the difficulty.
why: The wrong options each flatten three distinct categories into one, which is the recurring error in synthesis items.
trapnote: Multi-limb chains rarely share one category. Classify each limb before tracing the chain.

q: A set of statements on the definition of the State is accurate but adds that the strength of the lower House is a component of that definition. Which statement is correct?
options: The added statement is defective: House strength is a structural provision
The added statement is accurate: the House is an organ of the State
The added statement is defective: House strength belongs to the Directive Principles
The added statement is accurate for the purposes of writ jurisdiction alone
expl: Composition of the House is a structural matter unconnected with the definition.
why: The second option exploits the overlap in ordinary language between the State as an entity and its organs.
trapnote: A true-sounding overlap in ordinary language is the usual disguise for a planted item.

q: The November 2022 ruling is cited to fix the strength of the lower House. Which statement is correct?
options: The citation succeeds: the ruling set the outer limit of House strength
The citation fails: House strength was fixed by the same ruling in 2024
The citation succeeds subject to the completion of the next delimitation
The citation fails: the ruling concerned reservation, not House composition
expl: The ruling concerned the economic reservation and the ceiling doctrine alone.
why: The fourth option adds the delimitation condition from an unrelated amendment, a frequent cross-contamination.
trapnote: Check the subject-matter of a ruling before accepting any proposition drawn from it.

q: The 2024 ruling is cited to describe all university land as a community resource. Which statement is correct?
options: The citation succeeds: all institutional land was so classified by the ruling
The citation fails: the ruling concerned only agricultural holdings
The citation fails: the ruling requires a test to be satisfied in each case
The citation succeeds where the institution receives any government aid
expl: The ruling imposed a test rather than a blanket classification.
why: The third option narrows the ruling incorrectly, which is the opposite error to the citation being tested.
trapnote: A ruling that imposes a test cannot be used for a blanket classification in either direction.

q: The 2023 reservation amendment is cited to claim immediate additional seats in the upper House. Which statement is correct?
options: The citation fails once: the amendment covers that House but awaits a census
The citation fails twice: the amendment excludes that House and awaits a census
The citation succeeds: the amendment is operative from the date of assent
The citation fails once: the amendment is operative but excludes that House
expl: The amendment covers directly elected Houses only and operates after a census and delimitation.
why: Two options identify one defect and miss the other, so partial knowledge produces a near miss rather than an error.
trapnote: Two independent limbs here: which Houses are covered, and when the amendment operates.

q: The criminal statutes in force from July 2024 are cited to dispense with production before a magistrate. Which statement is correct?
options: The citation fails: production is retained and is in any event a constitutional guarantee
The citation succeeds: the new statutes replaced production with a reporting requirement
The citation fails: production was retained only for offences punishable with death
The citation succeeds where the arrest is made outside the local jurisdiction
expl: Production was retained, and the guarantee exists independently of the statute.
why: The fourth option ties the safeguard to the jurisdiction-free registration provision, which concerns a different subject.
trapnote: A constitutional guarantee does not depend on a statute restating it.

q: The 2022 creation of twenty-six districts is cited as a basis for determining citizenship locally. Which statement is correct?
options: The citation succeeds: district authorities determine status within their areas
The citation fails: status is determined by the State government alone
The citation succeeds where the person has resided in the district for five years
The citation fails: reorganisation is administrative and status rests elsewhere
expl: Reorganisation alters administration; citizenship rests on the Constitution and the statute.
why: The third option reaches the right conclusion by naming the wrong authority, which is a separate error.
trapnote: A correct conclusion with a wrong authority named is still a wrong option.
